newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy mini-budget may come soon - govt official.
newsitem.headline: Italy mini-budget may come soon - govt official.

text.p: Italy may need a supplementary budget to plug its 1996 deficit overshoot and it could be drawn up sooner than expected, a senior government official said.
Cabinet undersecretary Enrico Micheli, in a television interview on Wednesday night, repeated the centre-left government line that any mini-budget would be consist of spending cuts.
He said the government would have to review official data to determine whether a mini-budget was needed and that the "next days (and) the next weeks" would be important in the process.
"Perhaps we should not even wait for the quarterly accounts to reach a conclusion," Micheli said.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi has said previously that no steps would be taken until the quarterly accounts were published, probably in March.
Micheli, who is Prodi's chief cabinet aide, said any supplementary budget would be "balanced."
He said "we will certainly have to act from the point of view of cuts."
Treasury Ministry estimates published last week showed a 1996 public deficit of 138.5 trillion lire, above a revised government target of 123.0 trillion lire for the year.
Prodi has drawn up a tough 62.5 trillion lire budget for 1997 to try to ensure Italy makes the grade for membership of Europe's planned single currency.

Many economists say extra measures will be needed because of last year's overshoot to keep the deficit in check. Independent estimates cited on Italian radio on Thursday were for a supplementary budget of 20 trillion to 25 trillion lire.
